issue: Four mutually inconsistent pipeline universes (21, 25, 71, 98 IDs)
reason: The 25-row file was bounded by a page break in the source PDF, not by any inclusion criterion; it is Operational CC rows 1-16 plus all 10 UC CC, missing page 4. None of the four had a stated rule.
source: 20251231_NGPL.pdf, all 9 tables; totals reconcile to the register's own page-1 subtotals

issue: Start Point / End Point / Intermediate Points are not in the source
correction: field removed; 63 names published in unsourced_locations.csv
reason: Full-text search of the register found 39 of the names nowhere in it; ~10 more occur only as CGD Geographical Area names, which are not route points.
source: 20251231_NGPL.pdf full-text search

issue: Node coordinates of unknown provenance, 4 badly wrong
reason: Selecting among in-state homonyms by population placed Hazira 945 km from the true location. Rule replaced: unique in-state match, or independent agreement within 25 km, else AMBIGUOUS.
source: GeoNames IN.txt, state-constrained; legacy table used only to corroborate

issue: Vijaipur, Mallavaram, Jagdishpur misplaced
reason: Same population-tiebreak defect as Hazira. Vijaipur has no populated-place entry at all and is now unresolved rather than guessed.
source: GeoNames IN.txt; 04_geocode_nodes.py

issue: A Category-C derived count inside a Category-A table, and wrong
reason: Counting on '&' split single state names: 'UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu' is one state, 'Meghalaya & Sikkim' is two. True values 3 and 2. Now computed on demand by ngpl_paths.normalise_states().
source: 20251231_NGPL.pdf states column, read verbatim

issue: Reconstructed curved routes leave Indian territory
original: 17.20 passes 40 km inside Nepal and 400 km into the Bay of Bengal; 17.05 reaches 130 km into the Arabian Sea
reason: Free Bezier arcs, not alignments. Only 28% of 17.05 and 35% of 17.20 intersected Indian land. All layers derived from them are invalidated.
source: Geometric inspection against national boundary

issue: 'Kanai - Chhata - Panitar' read as three waypoints
reason: 'Kanai Chhata' is a single locality near Contai, Purba Medinipur, West Bengal. The Dec-2025 register cannot settle this on its own, so the split is externally sourced and cited.
source: PNGRB NGPL register 02-12-2022 release; Global Energy Monitor gem.wiki

issue: Validator reported success on a partial run
correction: skips tracked as first-class; prints INCOMPLETE and exits 1
reason: The two skipped groups were the only ones comparing the master against an independent source. Internal consistency alone passes on a silently altered value.
source: Mutation testing: 13 corrupted masters, 2 initially passed

issue: Reported '0 nodes disagree with legacy by >25 km' when zero comparisons had run
correction: DID NOT RUN, reported as a non-pass
reason: Legacy files were not found under the hard-coded names. A check that did not run was rendered as a check that passed - the third occurrence of this failure mode on this project.
source: Direct inspection after the reported result proved unreproducible

issue: No honest route geometry existed after the curved arcs were rejected
reason: Built only between resolved nodes. Gapped pairs contribute no geometry, so a route broken by an unresolved node is visibly discontinuous rather than silently bridged.
source: pipeline_nodes.csv (GeoNames, state-constrained) + pipeline titles in 20251231_NGPL.pdf

issue: NA-discipline checks silently tested nothing
reason: Pandas' default na_values contains the literal string 'NA'. Four checks whose purpose is to stop a missing value being written as 0 were comparing against the wrong string.
source: Found by fixture run; 14/14 mutations now caught

issue: Package could not be regenerated from itself
reason: Outputs were distributed without the code that produced them. A data package whose outputs cannot be regenerated fails reproducibility review regardless of how well the outputs validate.
source: Directory listing of the delivered package

issue: Twelve hard-coded copies of the package root; three divergent state normalisers
reason: The hard-coded default assumed Colab and Drive in a package also run from a Windows desktop. The duplicated normaliser was separately buggy in each copy.
source: Consolidation; normaliser regression-tested on all known compound state names

issue: The link between the transmission network and the CGD networks was never transcribed
correction: 115 tap-off rows from register pages 9-13 and 17-18
reason: The STPL tables are the only place the register connects trunk pipelines to distribution areas. Transcribed as literal data; correctness demonstrated by reproducing the register's printed 558 km total for each of the two tables.
source: 20251231_NGPL.pdf pp. 9-13 (operational, 558.032 km) and pp. 17-18 (under construction, 557.802 km)

issue: A tap-off could be re-pointed at a different pipeline of the same operator without any check failing
correction: holds the register's own name, copied from pipeline_master.csv
reason: Found by mutation testing: changing 17.03 to 17.20 passed every check because both are GAIL. Exact equality between id and name now catches it (O-13).
source: Mutation test, 15 corrupted copies

issue: Route points missing from pipeline names were suspected but not demonstrated
original: flagged only as a high length ratio, cause unknown
correction: 8 pipelines proven from the register's own two columns; 4 explicitly excluded as inconclusive
reason: The register states route points in the pipeline name and states crossed in a separate column. Where a recorded state cannot be entered by any named point, the name is incomplete. Source-internal and verifiable from the public PDF without code.
source: 20251231_NGPL.pdf, pipeline names and States Covered column; corroborated by the acronym ETBPNMTPL for 5.08 on p.17

issue: No edge list existed; the 8 connections with no geometry risked being dropped
reason: Dropping geometry-less edges would make the network appear better connected than the register states and would delete Vijaipur, an interconnection on three pipelines, from the topology entirely.
source: route_segments.csv + pipeline names in 20251231_NGPL.pdf

issue: The dataset described a network but never analysed it
correction: 56 nodes with centrality, cut-point status and node-removal impact, every metric computed twice
reason: Every figure is given over the topology the register states AND over the topology the dataset can draw. Reporting only the drawable graph would claim the network is broken where in fact the data is; reporting only the stated graph would overstate what the dataset supports. The difference between them is the uncertainty caused by the five unlocated nodes.
source: pipeline_edges.csv + pipeline_nodes.csv; algorithms cross-checked against networkx

issue: Hand-written Brandes betweenness was exactly 2x the correct value
reason: On an undirected graph Brandes visits every pair from both ends, so the accumulated score must be halved before normalising. No rank changed, so the printed report looked correct; found only by the independent networkx cross-check in 15_validate_vulnerability.py.
source: networkx betweenness_centrality(normalized=True), agreement now within 1e-6

issue: Treating pipelines that share a place name as physically connected is an inference the register never states
correction: stated on every row of both vulnerability tables
reason: Uran is named by four pipelines, so the graph has them meeting there. If any pair passes through without a tie-in, the graph contains a connection that does not exist and every centrality figure shifts. Recorded as the largest threat to this step's validity.
source: README 8.10
